meta.note: Dated windows come from the organisers' own sites, read on 5 September 2026. The pressure level is my own judgement as a Berlin guide, not a price feed.

windows.name: IFA Berlin
windows.reader: Europe's big consumer technology fair. Trade and private visitors both attend, so five days of hotel demand land in City West and spill east into Mitte.

windows.name: Berlin Art Week
windows.where: Galleries and museums across the city
windows.reader: Good week to be here. The crowd is spread over dozens of small venues rather than one hall, so it changes what is open in the evening more than what a room costs.

windows.name: InnoTrans
windows.reader: The rail industry fair, every two years. Almost entirely business travellers on expense accounts, which is exactly the crowd that empties the mid-range hotels first.

windows.name: BMW Berlin-Marathon
windows.where: Straight through the centre, finish at the Brandenburg Gate
windows.reader: Runners book months ahead and bring family. The Sunday route closes roads through Mitte and Tiergarten until the afternoon, so plan a walking day, not a driving one.

windows.name: German Unity Day
windows.where: Brandenburg Gate and Unter den Linden
windows.reader: Germans travel domestically on this weekend and the centre carries a public programme. Museums and sights are open, most shops are not.

windows.name: Festival of Lights
windows.where: Landmarks across the centre, after dark
windows.reader: Ten evenings of projections on the Dom, the Rathaus and the Gate. Daytime feels normal; the pressure is on the evening, on the trains after 20:00 and on the two weekends.

windows.name: Christmas market season
windows.where: Humboldt Forum, Gendarmenmarkt, and dozens more
windows.size: Weekends are the peak, not the weekdays
windows.reader: The Humboldt Forum market runs 18 November to 3 January. A Tuesday in early December is calm. The three weekends before Christmas are the busiest shopping days of the Berlin year.

windows.name: New Year's Eve
windows.size: The single most expensive night of the year
windows.reader: Hotels sell minimum-stay packages and the centre is fenced for the Gate party. If you only want the fireworks, you can see plenty from any bridge.

windows.name: Grüne Woche
windows.reader: The food and farming fair, open to the public and busy every single day for ten days. It turns the quietest month in Berlin into a booked-out one.

windows.name: Fruit Logistica
windows.reader: Three days, trade badges only, so it never touches the sights. It does take rooms, and it lands in the week before the Berlinale.

windows.name: Berlinale
windows.where: Potsdamer Platz and cinemas across the city
windows.reader: The film market runs 10 to 16 February and fills hotels with industry guests. The two public audience days are 20 and 21 February, when tickets are easiest to get.

windows.name: ITB Berlin
windows.size: The world's largest travel trade show
windows.reader: Trade only, and the whole global travel industry is in town. Of every week in the calendar this is the one where a normal visitor gets the worst room for the money.

windows.name: Lollapalooza Berlin
windows.reader: A weekend festival out at the Olympiastadion. The centre keeps working normally; the S-Bahn to Westend does not.

undated.name: CSD Berlin, the Pride demonstration
undated.usual: Traditionally the fourth Saturday of July
undated.note: The 2025 demonstration was on 26 July. No 2027 date published yet.

undated.name: Karneval der Kulturen
undated.usual: The Whitsun weekend, which in 2027 is 14 to 17 May
undated.note: Whit Monday, 17 May 2027, is a public holiday in Berlin. The organisers have not published the 2027 dates.

undated.name: DFB-Pokal final
undated.note: Two travelling fanbases arrive for one Saturday. Not announced for 2027.

undated.name: Formula E Berlin E-Prix
undated.usual: Spring, on the old Tempelhof airport apron
undated.note: The 2027 calendar is not published yet.
